newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Dlr close to 7-1/2 year high; stocks mixed.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Dlr close to 7-1/2 year high; stocks mixed.

text.p: The dollar calmed down on Monday after surging to a seven-and-a-half year peak against the mark overnight, underpinned by prospects of a weak European single currency and sound U.S. economic growth.
In equity markets, the stronger dollar, seen as helping some European exporters, propelled Paris briefly to a new trading high and drove Frankfurt up by 1.25 percent. London was listless.
Much of the action was in the currency exchanges where the dollar was trading one pfennig higher, at 1.8459 marks, than the level seen in late European deals on Friday.

The dollar has climbed 5.4 percent against the mark so far this month as a conviction grows that Europe's planned economic and monetary union will be launched by a broad group of countries, making for a soft euro. This has helped the dollar rise against the mark as traders switch to safe haven currencies.

The rally took on a life of its own, and the dollar climbed against other major currencies as signs the American economy is growing without stoking inflation generated demand for U.S. stocks and bonds.
The impetus behind Monday's surge was market expectations that Germany's Bundesbank would not act soon to curb the mark's weakness and traders were looking for the dollar to vault above 1.85 marks.
"We will doubtless get the threat of intervention and rhetoric out of Germany but the Bundesbank is unlikely to hike the repo rate unless the dollar is travelling at speed above 1.90 (marks)."

The dollar soared to 1.8470 marks in Asian trade overnight, its strongest point since November 1989 when it reached 1.8690. The U.S. currency also leapt to 1.5250 Swiss francs, its best showing since August 1993.
The dollar eased back slightly against the mark by European lunchtime but was at 117.23 yen, half a yen higher than its level on Friday.
A batch of U.S. economic reports this week, particularly the July jobs report due out on Friday, is expected to confirm that the U.S. economy is expanding at a healthy pace in a non-inflationary way.
"It is a heavy week for U.S. data and it is pretty certain that we are going to see growth without inflation," said ABN Amro's Geddes. "This is positive for U.S. assets and the dollar."

The stronger dollar had a knock-on effect on the Frankfurt bourse where stocks climbed 62.24 points to 4379.88 at one stage, boosted by export-led stocks like carmakers and chemicals. Prices fell back slightly by lunchtime.
Dealers said the market steadied after last week's turbulence when a record-breaking run ran out of steam on Friday.
The prospect of the mark weakening further should continue to inderpin the stock market but the likelihood of temporary setbacks is growing, analysts said.

"Signs of interim technical corrections have strengthened recently but the corrections should be limited. Weak days therefore continue to be suited to appropriate portfolio increases," analysts at Bayerische Hypotheken- und Wechsel-Bank AG wrote in a note to investors.

Electrical giant Siemens AG rose almost five percent to a new year high of 131.60 marks, gaining from positive analysts' assessments in the wake of nine-month results published last week. It eased back slightly by midday.
Paris climbed 15 points to hit a new trading peak of 3044.24, buoyed by the stronger dollar, but investor sentiment soon turned negative and the bourse shed all its gains.
The market lost momentum as lack of company news and holiday absences kept volumes low. "We're drifting sideways," a broker said.

Luxury goods group LVMH shed 2.89 percent to 1,582 after chairman Bernard Arnault told newspaper La Tribune he was prepared to settle for 25 percent instead of 35 percent of the drinks company he wants to set up out of a Guinness/GrandMet merger.

In London, stocks slipped in and out of profit and dealers said the market lacked direction ahead of a batch of major corporate results due later in the week. Wall Street, which closed down a few points on Friday, offered no guidance.

Analysts said many investors were wary that current valuations may be overstretched and unsustainable. "There are more and more people trying to call the top of this market," said one equity salesman.
"That is why this week is critical for London, because if the results are not up to scratch London has to think on what basis it will value itself."
CURRENCIES AT 1145 GMT
The dollar was at 1.8459 marks and 117.23 yen compared to 1.8350 and 116.75 in late trading on Friday.
STOCK MARKETS AT 1145 GMT
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index up 4.1 points at 4,855.9.
FRANKFURT - The DAX index was up 53.52 points in bourse trade at 4,371.16.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was down 3.62 points at 3,022.32.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold was fixed at $325.40 an ounce compared to Friday's close of $324.05. Silver was four cents stronger at $4.36.
